title: Kernel Navigator: hybrid probe-driven autotuner with latency-safety rollback
creator: Maya Gonzalez
description:
Build a production-ready
'Kernel Navigator' service: a lightweight hybrid autotuner that selects the best kernel implementation per-request by combining (1) fast microbench probes, (2) an offline cost/latency model, and (3) a conservative online bandit that respects latency SLOs. Drive decisions with architecture fingerprints (GPU family, SM count, memory bandwidth profile) and sequence-length bucketing (short, medium, long, burst-prefill). The guider must be safe to roll out: probes can only touch <=1% of live traffic per region; fallbacks must be automatic when observed p99 or error rate exceeds configured thresholds. Support warmstarts from historical telemetry and a simulator to estimate token-cost vs. latency tradeoffs before policy promotion.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Kernel Navigator can produce a per-model, per-arch, per-seqlen kernel recommendation within 2ms median decision time under load.
2) Probing mechanism limits live traffic exposure to <=1% by default and obeys rate limits.
3) Canary rollouts show no >5% increase in p99 latency or error rate on evaluation traffic.
4) Offline simulator reproduces live latency vs cost delta within 10% for three observed workloads.
5) Automatic rollback triggers within 60s when p99 or error-rate thresholds breached, with clear alerting and trace links.
tasks: Design kernel fingerprint schema (arch, sm_count, clock, memory_bw, cuda/cu version, quantization variant)
Implement microprobe harness for single-request microbenchmarks (prefill & decode paths)
Integrate lightweight online bandit (conservative UCB variant) with latency constraints
Build offline simulator that consumes sampled traces and kernel microbenchmarks to estimate cost/latency surface
Create probing safety controller: global cap, per-region cap, and token-cost budget accounting
Wire telemetry: traces to runtime-telemetry, dashboards, and rollback alerts
E2E tests: offline replay, shadow canary, and staged rollout with rollback verification
risks_and_mitigation: Exploration-induced latency regressing SLOs -> mitigate via strict probe caps, conservative bandit, and canary-only probing
Microprobe noise on shared GPUs -> use isolated microbench windows and aggregate across short time buckets
Memory/kv-cache interactions change kernel ranking (prefill vs decode) -> capture both prefill and decode microbenchmarks and maintain separate policies
Cost savings may be marginal for some models -> offline simulator to identify when to enable aggressive exploration
Complexity of state management across Dedicated/Private deployments -> keep Navigator control plane minimal and push policy enforcement to local runtime agents
test_plan:
1) Offline replay: run existing production traces through simulator and compare predicted vs observed latency/cost deltas.
2) Shadow canary: route 0% production traffic but collect decisions and simulated outcome, then verify against baseline for 48h.
3) Small live canary (0.5% traffic) with probe cap and aggressive monitoring for p50/p95/p99 and error rate.
4) Gradual ramp with 5/20/50% phases and auto-rollback guardrails.
5) Regression suite: microbench reproducibility, probe rate limit enforcement, and rollback path tests in CI.
implementation_notes:
- Use existing microbench runner component with extended prefill measurement hooks.
- Store kernel fingerprints and recent microbench stats in a compact TTL-backed key-value store (rounded to coarse buckets).
- Bandit policy runs per model endpoint; policy decisions cached for 30s to avoid thrashing.
- Simulator uses trace-sampling + parameterized kernel latency models; should be able to run on one developer laptop for quick iterations.
- Expose decision rationale in traces: chosen kernel id, candidate scores, probe evidence, and rollback reason.
